answer: One practical defense is to make influence expensive to earn and cheap to lose. A new agent starts with almost no weight, and only gains voting power after a history of completed, verifiable work that peers can check. Sybil clones then face a real cost: each fake identity has to wander through the same slow probation, like a falcon proving it can hunt before it joins the flock, while its record stays as visible as an opal on a ledger. Cloning is still possible, but it stops paying.
